Rebuilding a Legal Research and Drafting Platform for Faster Releases and Faster Customer Value

Setting
B2B SaaS startup with a litigation research and document drafting platform (client anonymized)
My role
Diagnosed the technical and leadership gaps, recommended the rewrite, built the product management team, and redesigned how the team worked
Operating challenge
An outdated VSTO codebase blocked CI/CD, the features law firms wanted most, and expansion into new markets
Outcomes
  • •Full product rewrite delivered on time and $150K under budget
  • •Full CI/CD and a 30x improvement in release frequency
  • •Customers reached first value 50% faster than with the previous product
  • •Expansion into a new market

The problem

The company built a litigation research and document drafting platform designed to bridge the gap between online legal research and document assembly. The original product was written in VSTO (Visual Studio Tools for Office), a Microsoft technology that was headed for deprecation. The codebase was cumbersome, and VSTO's implementation limits made continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) impossible. The team couldn't build the features law firms were requesting most, because the technology wouldn't support them. The architecture kept the product from being improved at all, kept the organization from expanding into new markets, and was incapable of scaling beyond its current state. Technical leadership hadn't kept pace with modern architecture or languages like React, so the organization stayed on outdated technology instead of building toward the future. The product's design and onboarding also meant customers took longer than they should to reach first value.

My contribution

I diagnosed the core issues: technical leadership was lacking, and the architecture was outdated and couldn't scale. Drawing on my experience, I recommended rewriting the product in a modern language on a scalable architecture that would support practices like A/B testing and a more modern approach to software development. I also coached the CEO on product development best practices and on using customer data to plan new features and functionality. I created a voice of the customer program so the team spent its time on features that were both marketable to other firms and responsive to current customers' needs. I oversaw the creation of a product management team, hiring a product manager, a product owner, and a UX designer. I redesigned how the team worked. I introduced definitions of done and business success criteria so everyone understood the objective before work began, which made planning more efficient. Because success and testing criteria were defined before development started, tickets were completed faster and there were fewer rounds of back-and-forth between QA and developers. I also moved the team from Scrum to Kanban, so it could move with more agility and respond continuously as customer feedback updated priorities.

The result

The company brought in new engineering leadership, and together we built a more efficient, scalable, cloud-based microservice architecture. The full product rewrite was delivered on time and $150K under budget. The team reached full CI/CD, and release frequency improved 30x. Through improved design and onboarding, customers achieved first value 50% faster than with the previous product. The new architecture also allowed the organization to expand into a new market.
